Neha — quick technical run-through and what we can package in the evidence PDF: 

- No-adaptive-learning toggle: We have a per-tenant configuration flag in the control plane. When set to 'opt-out', telemetry is still collected for runtime metrics (latency/errors) but training telemetry and any pipeline that writes to our model-improvement queues is disabled. This is enforced at router/kernel selection points; there is no automated snapshot into training datasets while the toggle is set.

- Prompt/response retention: By default we keep ephemeral traces for 7 days for debugging; for no-learning customers we can reduce to 24 hours and mark them as non-persistent. We can also provide an SFTP export of all prompt/response pairs for a given date range (CSV gz) to MedLine's custody SFTP. Export tooling logs the job run, artifact checksum, and delivery timestamp.

- KV / cache: KV cache entries are ephemeral and not used for training. For full assurance we can enable an additional onshore-only KV zone that never leaves the selected region and is excluded from telemetry exports.

- Encryption & access: All artifacts are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS (optional for Private). Transfer to SFTP uses TLS + server fingerprint verification. Access logs are retained per our retention schedule and we can provide a redacted sample access log for audit.

I put together a short ops evidence checklist and a custody_matrix_v1.xlsx (attached). We can produce the formal PDF (ops_evidence_checklist.pdf) by Fri EOD if legal confirms scope language.

--David
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
